claims.text: TOR-TILD's conventional EAM references inadequately represent the diverse liquid configurations of high-entropy alloys and consequently exhibit significant thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
An ML interatomic potential can be trained on high-temperature ab initio liquid configurations of a multicomponent high-entropy material.
Ab initio-trained ML potentials are applicable to refractory multi-principal-element alloys.
Training an ML potential on high-temperature liquid configurations will improve its representation of the liquid's configurational diversity.
The proposed ML potential captures many-body interactions and the diversity of local atomic environments.
Improved representation of liquid configurations enhances reference-target phase-space overlap.
Enhanced phase-space overlap reduces thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The proposed ML reference will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by approximately a factor of 2–3 relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
A potential trained specifically on liquid configurations will improve free-energy estimates for both solid and liquid phases relative to EAM references.
The intervention applies to equiatomic or near-equiatomic multicomponent high-entropy alloys, including quinary systems.
The applicable temperature interval is approximately 0.95–1.05 times the alloy melting temperature.
The advantage of the ML reference may diminish at lower temperatures or in less compositionally complex systems where EAM may already be adequate.
Evidence from elemental and binary systems supports the effectiveness of ML potentials for this purpose.
